messages.subject: [R-sig-Fedora] Install R on Redhat EL6.5 without internet - issue
messages.subject_clean: Install R on Redhat EL6.5 without internet - issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Sorry if this email does not concern you, but I needed help to install R
and R-Studio on a Redhat Linux Enterprise Server WITHOUT Internet
connection.

I have a Mac and can scp rpm packages to the RedHat server.
I have gone through almost all of the options that google returned but none
helped me.

Even after installing the EPEL package, i get the following error :
"Cannot retrieve repository metadata (repomd.xml) for repository: HDP-2.3.
Please verify its path and try again "

I can see that the EPEL package did install on the server but the YUM
command is not able to find the EPEL repo.

Can someone please help as this is really urgent. Thanks in advance.

Regards,
Shankar

	[[alternative HTML version deleted]]

messages.body_plain:

         I??d like to install R-3.3.2 from .tar.gz on my linux system(CentOS 6.4). When installing, R told me that the version of zlib was too old.

         So, I eager to know which version of zlib did R-3.3.2 software examine at its configure step. How could I check the version of zlib? I will appreciate a lot if you could do me a favour.

messages.subject: [R-sig-Fedora] how can I know the version of my zlib checked by R
messages.subject_clean: how can I know the version of my zlib checked by R
messages.body_plain:
On Tue, 2017-02-07 at 08:39 +0000, nw?? wrote:
> Hi, professors
> 
> ?????????I'd like to install R-3.3.2 from .tar.gz on my linux
> system(CentOS 6.4). When installing, R told me that the version of
> zlib was too old.

Do you really need to install from source? The EPEL RPMs by Tom
Callaway from Redhat contain a bundled version of zlib for platforms
that do not have an up-to-date system version, and so are much easier
to install.

Note that it is not only zlib that is affected. You will have the same
issue for bzip, xzv, pcre, and curl.

> ?????????So, I eager to know which version of zlib did R-3.3.2
> software examine at its configure step. How could I check the version
> of zlib? I will appreciate a lot if you could do me a favour.

This information is contained in the "R Installation and
Administration" manual, also known as "R-admin". The minimum version
required is zlib 1.2.5. ?You can also see this information in the
output from configure, e.g. on my system:

checking if zlib version >= 1.2.5... yes

Martyn

> Best Regards
> 
> Wei Ning
> Ctrip, Shanghai
